name: Hobart, Tasmania 🇦🇺
subtitle: Australia's most exciting food city — wild produce, wild chefs
items: The Agrarian Kitchen (New Norfolk — destination dining, produce from their farm)
Peppina (Tasman Hotel, Chef Massimo Mele — best Italian in Tasmania)
Restaurant Maria (waterfront, Tasmanian twist on Lisbon & Lebanon, Chef Christian Ryan co-owner)
Aløft (riverside, Chef Christian Ryan — Scandi-influenced seasonal)
Scholé (10-seater, Chef Luke Burgess, ever-changing seasonal menu)
Six Russell Bistro (Sandy Bay, Chef Kobi Ruzicka — opened 2025 to acclaim)
Dier Makr (wine bar + bistro, Kobi Ruzicka — natural wine anchor)
Lucinda (wine bar, same Ruzicka universe — great list)
Franklin (Brooke St Pier, wood-fired)
Templo (intimate Italian, 20-seater, small plates)
Born In Brunswick (North Hobart café, Melbourne-style coffee + brunch)
Battery Point Bakery (old-school — pies, danishes, egg & bacon)
Jackman & McRoss Bakery (Battery Point, artisan)
Pilgrim Coffee (best espresso in Hobart)
Farm Gate Market (Sunday, Bathurst St — the best of Tasmanian produce)
Barilla Bay Oysters (drive-in oyster bar, airport road)
Smolt Kitchen & Bar (Salamanca, waterfront)
Me Wah (Cantonese, Wrest Point — the 40-year institution)
Aloft Bar (views, cocktails, pre-dinner)
MONA (Museum of Old & New Art café + restaurant — the experience)
